sanskrit: kāmaṃ tu naḥ sveṣu guṇeṣu saṅgaḥ; kāmaṃ ca nānyonyaguṇopalabdhiḥ asmān ṛte nāsti tavopalabdhis; tvām apy ṛte 'smān na bhajeta harṣaḥ
english: Granted, we are each attached to our own qualities, and granted, we do not perceive one another's qualities. Yet without us there is no perception for you, and without you no joy could attend upon us either.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam subhage pañcahotṝṇāṃ vidhānam iha yādṛśam
english: The Brāhmaṇa said: On this point too they recite an ancient tale, O fortunate one, concerning what the disposition of the five oblation-priests is here.

sanskrit: prāṇāpānāv udānaś ca samāno vyāna eva ca pañcahotṝn athaitān vai paraṃ bhāvaṃ vidur budhāḥ
english: The prāṇa and the apāna, the udāna, the samāna, and the vyāna—these the wise know as the five oblation-priests and as the supreme state of being.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca svabhāvāt sapta hotāra iti te pūrvikā matiḥ yathā vai pañca hotāraḥ paro bhāvas tathocyatām
english: The Brāhmaṇī said: Your earlier opinion held that by nature there are seven oblation-priests. Now tell me how the five oblation-priests are the supreme state of being.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca prāṇena saṃbhṛto vāyur apāno jāyate tataḥ apāne saṃbhṛto vāyus tato vyānaḥ pravartate
english: The Brāhmaṇa said: The vital air gathered up by the prāṇa is born as the apāna; the air gathered up in the apāna gives rise then to the vyāna.

sanskrit: vyānena saṃbhṛto vāyus tatodānaḥ pravartate udāne saṃbhṛto vāyuḥ samānaḥ saṃpravartate
english: The air gathered up by the vyāna gives rise then to the udāna; the air gathered up in the udāna brings the samāna fully into play.

sanskrit: te 'pṛcchanta purā gatvā pūrvajātaṃ prajāpatim yo no jyeṣṭhas tam ācakṣva sa naḥ śreṣṭho bhaviṣyati
english: Of old they went and asked Prajāpati, the firstborn: 'Tell us which of us is the eldest; he shall be our foremost.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca yasmin pralīne pralayaṃ vrajanti; sarve prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śarīre yasmin pracīrṇe ca punaś caranti; sa vai śreṣṭho gacchata yatra kāmaḥ
english: Brahmā said: He upon whose dissolution all the vital breaths in the bodies of breathing creatures go to dissolution, and upon whose moving forth they move once more—he indeed is the foremost. Go now wherever you please.

sanskrit: prāṇa uvāca mayi pralīne pralayaṃ vrajanti; sarve prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śarīre mayi pracīrṇe ca punaś caranti; śreṣṭho hy ahaṃ paśyata māṃ pralīnam
english: The prāṇa said: When I dissolve, all the vital breaths in the bodies of breathing creatures go to dissolution, and when I move forth they move once more. I am the foremost—behold me as I dissolve.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca prāṇaḥ pralīyata tataḥ punaś ca pracacāra ha samānaś cāpy udānaś ca vaco 'brūtāṃ tataḥ śubhe
english: The Brāhmaṇa said: The prāṇa then dissolved and again moved forth; and the samāna and the udāna then spoke these words, O fair one.

sanskrit: na tvaṃ sarvam idaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasīha yathā vayam na tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'si naḥ prāṇa apāno hi vaśe tava pracacāra punaḥ prāṇas tam apāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: 'You do not stand here pervading all this as we do; you are not our foremost, O prāṇa, for the apāna is in your power.' Again the prāṇa moved forth, and the apāna addressed it.

sanskrit: mayi pralīne pralayaṃ vrajanti; sarve prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śarīre mayi pracīrṇe ca punaś caranti; śreṣṭho hy ahaṃ paśyata māṃ pralīnam
english: 'When I dissolve, all the vital breaths in the bodies of breathing creatures go to dissolution, and when I move forth they move once more. I am the foremost—behold me as I dissolve.'

sanskrit: vyānaś ca tam udānaś ca bhāṣamāṇam athocatuḥ apāna na tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'si prāṇo hi vaśagas tava
english: As the apāna was speaking, the vyāna and the udāna then said to it: 'O apāna, you are not the foremost, for the prāṇa is subject to you.'

sanskrit: apānaḥ pracacārātha vyānas taṃ punar abravīt śreṣṭho 'ham asmi sarveṣāṃ śrūyatāṃ yena hetunā
english: The apāna then moved forth, and the vyāna in turn declared: 'I am the foremost of all—hear the reason why.'

sanskrit: mayi pralīne pralayaṃ vrajanti; sarve prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śarīre mayi pracīrṇe ca punaś caranti; śreṣṭho hy ahaṃ paśyata māṃ pralīnam
english: 'When I dissolve, all the vital breaths in the bodies of breathing creatures go to dissolution, and when I move forth they move once more. I am the foremost—behold me as I dissolve.'

sanskrit: prālīyata tato vyānaḥ punaś ca pracacāra ha prāṇāpānāv udānaś ca samānaś ca tam abruvan na tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'si no vyāna samāno hi vaśe tava
english: The vyāna then dissolved and again moved forth; and the prāṇa, the apāna, the udāna, and the samāna said to it: 'You are not our foremost, O vyāna, for the samāna is in your power.'

sanskrit: pracacāra punar vyānaḥ samānaḥ punar abravīt śreṣṭho 'ham asmi sarveṣāṃ śrūyatāṃ yena hetunā
english: Again the vyāna moved forth, and the samāna in turn declared: 'I am the foremost of all—hear the reason why.'

sanskrit: mayi pralīne pralayaṃ vrajanti; sarve prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śarīre mayi pracīrṇe ca punaś caranti; śreṣṭho hy ahaṃ paśyata māṃ pralīnam
english: 'When I dissolve, all the vital breaths in the bodies of breathing creatures go to dissolution, and when I move forth they move once more. I am the foremost—behold me as I dissolve.'

sanskrit: tataḥ samānaḥ prālilye punaś ca pracacāra ha prāṇāpānāv udānaś ca vyānaś caiva tam abruvan samāna na tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'si vyāna eva vaśe tava
english: Then the samāna dissolved and again moved forth; and the prāṇa, the apāna, the udāna, and the vyāna said to it: 'O samāna, you are not the foremost, for the vyāna alone is in your power.'

sanskrit: samānaḥ pracacārātha udānas tam uvāca ha śreṣṭho 'ham asmi sarveṣāṃ śrūyatāṃ yena hetunā
english: The samāna then moved forth, and the udāna said to it: 'I am the foremost of all—hear the reason why.'

sanskrit: mayi pralīne pralayaṃ vrajanti; sarve prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śarīre mayi pracīrṇe ca punaś caranti; śreṣṭho hy ahaṃ paśyata māṃ pralīnam
english: 'When I dissolve, all the vital breaths in the bodies of breathing creatures go to dissolution, and when I move forth they move once more. I am the foremost—behold me as I dissolve.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prālīyatodānaḥ punaś ca pracacāra ha prāṇāpānau samānaś ca vyānaś caiva tam abruvan udāna na tvaṃ śreṣṭho 'si vyāna eva vaśe tava
english: Then the udāna dissolved and again moved forth; and the prāṇa, the apāna, the samāna, and the vyāna said to it: 'O udāna, you are not the foremost, for the vyāna alone is in your power.'

sanskrit: tatas tān abravīd brahmā samavetān prajāpatiḥ sarve śreṣṭhā na vā śreṣṭhāḥ sarve cānyonyadharmiṇaḥ sarve svaviṣaye śreṣṭhāḥ sarve cānyonyarakṣiṇaḥ
english: Then Brahmā the Prajāpati said to them as they stood gathered: 'You are all foremost, or none of you is foremost; all of you sustain one another's functions; each is foremost in its own domain, and all are guardians of one another.'

sanskrit: ekaḥ sthiraś cāsthiraś ca viśeṣāt pañca vāyavaḥ eka eva mamaivātmā bahudhāpy upacīyate
english: 'There is one, both steady and unsteady; by distinction there are five winds. There is but one Self, my own, though it is built up in manifold ways.'

sanskrit: parasparasya suhṛdo bhāvayantaḥ parasparam svasti vrajata bhadraṃ vo dhārayadhvaṃ parasparam
english: 'Being friends to one another, nourishing one another—go in peace, blessings upon you, and uphold one another.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradasya ca saṃvādam ṛṣer devamatasya ca
english: The Brāhmaṇa said: On this point too they recite an ancient tale, the dialogue of Nārada and the seer Devamata.

sanskrit: devamata uvāca jantoḥ saṃjāyamānasya kiṃ nu pūrvaṃ pravartate prāṇo 'pānaḥ samāno vā vyāno vodāna eva ca
english: Devamata said: When a creature is coming into being, which arises first—the prāṇa, the apāna, the samāna, the vyāna, or indeed the udāna?

sanskrit: nārada uvāca yenāyaṃ sṛjyate jantus tato 'nyaḥ pūrvam eti tam prāṇadvaṃdvaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ tiryagaṃ cordhvagaṃ ca yat
english: Nārada said: That by which this creature is brought forth—another goes before it. And the pairing of the breaths is to be understood, both that which moves crosswise and that which moves upward.

sanskrit: devamata uvāca kenāyaṃ sṛjyate jantuḥ kaś cānyaḥ pūrvam eti tam prāṇadvaṃdvaṃ ca me brūhi tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca niścayāt
english: Devamata said: By what is this creature brought forth, and which other goes before it? Tell me with certainty about the pairing of the breaths, the crosswise and the upward.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca saṃkalpāj jāyate harṣaḥ śabdād api ca jāyate rasāt saṃjāyate cāpi rūpād api ca jāyate
english: Nārada said: From intention joy is born, and from sound too it is born; it arises from taste as well, and from form too it is born.

sanskrit: sparśāt saṃjāyate cāpi gandhād api ca jāyate etad rūpam udānasya harṣo mithunasaṃbhavaḥ
english: It arises from touch as well, and from smell too it is born. This is the form of the udāna: joy, which springs from union.

sanskrit: kāmāt saṃjāyate śukraṃ kāmāt saṃjāyate rasaḥ samānavyānajanite sāmānye śukraśoṇite
english: From desire the seed arises, from desire the essence arises; the seed and the blood, held in common, are produced by the samāna and the vyāna.

sanskrit: śukrāc choṇitasaṃsṛṣṭāt pūrvaṃ prāṇaḥ pravartate prāṇena vikṛte śukre tato 'pānaḥ pravartate
english: From the seed mingled with the blood, the prāṇa first comes into play; and when the seed has been transformed by the prāṇa, the apāna then comes into play.

sanskrit: prāṇāpānāv idaṃ dvaṃdvam avāk cordhvaṃ ca gacchataḥ vyānaḥ samānaś caivobhau tiryag dvaṃdvatvam ucyate
english: The prāṇa and the apāna are this pair, going downward and upward; the vyāna and the samāna, both together, are called the crosswise pair.

sanskrit: agnir vai devatāḥ sarvā iti vedasya śāsanam saṃjāyate brāhmaṇeṣu jñānaṃ buddhisamanvitam
english: 'Agni is verily all the deities'—such is the teaching of the Veda; and among brāhmaṇas there arises knowledge attended by discernment.

sanskrit: tasya dhūmas tamorūpaṃ rajo bhasma suretasaḥ sattvaṃ saṃjāyate tasya yatra prakṣipyate haviḥ
english: Of that fire the smoke is the form of tamas, and its ash is rajas; from that fire of fine seed sattva arises, there where the oblation is cast.

sanskrit: āghārau samāno vyānaś ca iti yajñavido viduḥ prāṇāpānāv ājyabhāgau tayor madhye hutāśanaḥ etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: The two sprinklings of ghee are the samāna and the vyāna—so those versed in sacrifice know; the prāṇa and the apāna are the two portions of clarified butter, and between them is the devourer of oblations. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: nirdvaṃdvam iti yat tv etat tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: As for that which is free of all pairs of opposites, hear it now as I declare it.

sanskrit: ahorātram idaṃ dvaṃdvaṃ tayor madhye hutāśanaḥ etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: Day and night are this pair, and between them is the devourer of oblations. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: ubhe caivāyane dvaṃdvaṃ tayor madhye hutāśanaḥ etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: The two solstitial courses of the sun are a pair, and between them is the devourer of oblations. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: ubhe satyānṛte dvaṃdvaṃ tayor madhye hutāśanaḥ etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: Truth and falsehood, the two, are a pair, and between them is the devourer of oblations. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: ubhe śubhāśubhe dvaṃdvaṃ tayor madhye hutāśanaḥ etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: The good and the evil, the two, are a pair, and between them is the devourer of oblations. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: sac cāsac caiva tad dvaṃdvaṃ tayor madhye hutāśanaḥ etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: The existent and the non-existent are that pair, and between them is the devourer of oblations. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ samāno vyāno vyasyate karma tena tat tṛtīyaṃ tu samānena punar eva vyavasyate
english: First the samāna and the vyāna; by these the work is set in motion. The third part, again, is brought about once more by the samāna.

sanskrit: śāntyarthaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca śāntir brahma sanātanam etad rūpam udānasya paramaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ
english: For the sake of peace there is the Vāmadeva hymn, and peace is the eternal Brahman. This the brāhmaṇas know as the supreme form of the udāna.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam cāturhotravidhānasya vidhānam iha yādṛśam
english: The Brāhmaṇa said: On this point too they recite an ancient tale, concerning the nature of the disposition of the four-priest oblation here.

sanskrit: tasya sarvasya vidhivad vidhānam upadekṣyate śṛṇu me gadato bhadre rahasyam idam uttamam
english: The disposition of all of it shall be taught according to rule. Listen to me as I tell it, O blessed one—this is the highest mystery.

sanskrit: karaṇaṃ karma kartā ca mokṣa ity eva bhāmini catvāra ete hotāro yair idaṃ jagad āvṛtam
english: The instrument, the action, the agent, and release—O lovely one, these four are the oblation-priests by whom this world is enveloped.

sanskrit: hotṝṇāṃ sādhanaṃ caiva śṛṇu sarvam aśeṣataḥ ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuś ca tvak ca śrotraṃ ca pañcamam mano buddhiś ca saptaite vijñeyā guṇahetavaḥ
english: And hear too, in full and without remainder, the means of these oblation-priests: smell, the tongue, the eye, the skin, and hearing as the fifth, the mind, and the intellect—these seven are to be known as the causes of the qualities.

sanskrit: gandho rasaś ca rūpaṃ ca śabdaḥ sparśaś ca pañcamaḥ mantavyam atha boddhavyaṃ saptaite karmahetavaḥ
english: Smell, taste, form, sound, and touch as the fifth, the object of thought and the object of cognition—these seven are the causes of action.

sanskrit: ghrātā bhakṣayitā draṣṭā spraṣṭā śrotā ca pañcamaḥ mantā boddhā ca saptaite vijñeyāḥ kartṛhetavaḥ
english: The smeller, the taster, the seer, the toucher, and the hearer as the fifth, the thinker and the knower—these seven are to be known as the causes of the agent.

sanskrit: svaguṇaṃ bhakṣayanty ete guṇavantaḥ śubhāśubham ahaṃ ca nirguṇo 'treti saptaite mokṣahetavaḥ
english: These, possessed of qualities, consume their own object, good and evil; and the thought 'I am here without qualities'—these seven are the causes of release.

sanskrit: viduṣāṃ budhyamānānāṃ svaṃ svaṃ sthānaṃ yathāvidhi guṇās te devatābhūtāḥ satataṃ bhuñjate haviḥ
english: For the wise who understand, each in its own station according to rule, those qualities, having become deities, continually consume the oblation.

sanskrit: adan hy avidvān annāni mamatvenopapadyate ātmārthaṃ pācayan nityaṃ mamatvenopahanyate
english: The ignorant man, eating his foods, becomes attached to them through the sense of 'mine'; cooking ever for his own sake, he is destroyed through the sense of 'mine'.

sanskrit: abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaṃ caiva madyapānaṃ ca hanti tam sa cānnaṃ hanti tac cānnaṃ sa hatvā hanyate budhaḥ
english: The eating of what should not be eaten and the drinking of liquor destroy him; he destroys that food, and that food destroys him; having destroyed, the wise man is himself destroyed.

sanskrit: attā hy annam idaṃ vidvān punar janayatīśvaraḥ sa cānnāj jāyate tasmin sūkṣmo nāma vyatikramaḥ
english: The wise lord, the eater, brings forth this food again; and he is born from food—therein lies a subtle distinction.

sanskrit: manasā gamyate yac ca yac ca vācā nirudyate śrotreṇa śrūyate yac ca cakṣuṣā yac ca dṛśyate
english: That which is reached by the mind, and that which is uttered by speech, that which is heard by the ear, and that which is seen by the eye,

sanskrit: sparśena spṛśyate yac ca ghrāṇena ghrāyate ca yat manaḥṣaṣṭhāni saṃyamya havīṃṣy etāni sarvaśaḥ
english: and that which is touched by touch, and that which is smelled by smell—restraining all these wholly, with the mind as the sixth, as oblations.

sanskrit: guṇavatpāvako mahyaṃ dīpyate havyavāhanaḥ yogayajñaḥ pravṛtto me jñānabrahmamanodbhavaḥ prāṇastotro 'pānaśastraḥ sarvatyāgasudakṣiṇaḥ
english: For me the purifying fire, the bearer of oblations, blazes endowed with qualities; the sacrifice of yoga is set in motion for me, born of the knowledge of Brahman in the mind, with the prāṇa for its hymn of praise, the apāna for its recited verse, and the renunciation of all things for its rich priestly fee.

sanskrit: karmānumantā brahmā me kartādhvaryuḥ kṛtastutiḥ kṛtapraśāstā tac chāstram apavargo 'sya dakṣiṇā
english: The one who sanctions the act is my Brahman-priest, the agent is my Adhvaryu, the deed itself the hymn of praise, the doer the director, and that scripture; and final release is the priestly fee of this sacrifice.

sanskrit: ṛcaś cāpy atra śaṃsanti nārāyaṇavido janāḥ nārāyaṇāya devāya yad abadhnan paśūn purā
english: And here too the people learned in Nārāyaṇa recite verses about how of old they bound the sacrificial victims for the god Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tatra sāmāni gāyanti tāni cāhur nidarśanam devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ bhīru sarvātmānaṃ nibodha me
english: There they sing the Sāman chants, and these they declare to be the demonstration. Know from me, O timid one, the god Nārāyaṇa, the Self of all.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca ekaḥ śāstā na dvitīyo 'sti śāstā; yathā niyukto 'smi tathā carāmi hṛdy eṣa tiṣṭhan puruṣaḥ śāsti śāstā; tenaiva yuktaḥ pravaṇād ivodakam
english: The Brāhmaṇa said: There is one Ruler; there is no second ruler. As I am appointed, so do I act. This Person, dwelling in the heart, the Ruler, rules; impelled by him alone I move, like water running down a slope.

sanskrit: eko gurur nāsti tato dvitīyo; yo hṛcchayas tam aham anubravīmi tenānuśiṣṭā guruṇā sadaiva; parābhūtā dānavāḥ sarva eva
english: There is one Teacher; there is no second besides him. Him who dwells in the heart I now proclaim. By that Teacher, ever instructed, the Dānavas were one and all overcome.

sanskrit: eko bandhur nāsti tato dvitīyo; yo hṛcchayas tam aham anubravīmi tenānuśiṣṭā bāndhavā bandhumantaḥ; saptarṣayaḥ sapta divi prabhānti
english: There is one Kinsman; there is no second besides him. Him who dwells in the heart I now proclaim. By him instructed, kinsmen rich in kindred, the Seven Sages, shine sevenfold in the sky.

sanskrit: ekaḥ śrotā nāsti tato dvitīyo; yo hṛcchayas tam aham anubravīmi tasmin gurau guruvāsaṃ niruṣya; śakro gataḥ sarvalokāmaratvam
english: There is one Hearer; there is no second besides him. Him who dwells in the heart I now proclaim. Having dwelt his term of pupilage under that Teacher, Śakra attained immortality over all the worlds.

sanskrit: eko dveṣṭā nāsti tato dvitīyo; yo hṛcchayas tam aham anubravīmi tenānuśiṣṭā guruṇā sadaiva; lokadviṣṭāḥ pannagāḥ sarva eva
english: There is one Hater; there is no second besides him. Him who dwells in the heart I now proclaim. By that Teacher, ever instructed, the serpents were one and all made hateful to the world.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam prajāpatau pannagānāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca saṃvidam
english: On this point too they recite an ancient tale, the conference of the serpents and the divine seers in the presence of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: devarṣayaś ca nāgāś ca asurāś ca prajāpatim paryapṛcchann upāsīnāḥ śreyo naḥ procyatām iti
english: The divine seers, the Nāgas, and the Asuras, sitting in attendance, asked Prajāpati: 'Let what is good for us be declared.'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ provāca bhagavāñ śreyaḥ samanupṛcchatām om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma te śrutvā prādravan diśaḥ
english: To them as they inquired after the good, the Blessed One spoke the single syllable Om, which is Brahman; and having heard it they ran off in all directions.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prādravamāṇānām upadeśārtham ātmanaḥ sarpāṇāṃ daśane bhāvaḥ pravṛttaḥ pūrvam eva tu
english: As they ran off, each taking the instruction for himself, in the serpents the disposition toward biting came forth first of all.

sanskrit: asurāṇāṃ pravṛttas tu dambhabhāvaḥ svabhāvajaḥ dānaṃ devā vyavasitā damam eva maharṣayaḥ
english: In the Asuras the disposition toward arrogance, born of their nature, came forth; the gods resolved upon giving, and the great seers upon self-restraint.

sanskrit: ekaṃ śāstāram āsādya śabdenaikena saṃskṛtāḥ nānā vyavasitāḥ sarve sarpadevarṣidānavāḥ
english: Approaching one Ruler, refined by one and the same sound, the serpents, divine seers, and Dānavas all resolved upon diverse things.

sanskrit: śṛṇoty ayaṃ procyamānaṃ gṛhṇāti ca yathātatham pṛcchatas tāvato bhūyo gurur anyo 'numanyate
english: This one hears what is being told and grasps it just as it is; and when he asks again and again, another, the inner Teacher, gives his assent.

sanskrit: tasya cānumate karma tataḥ paścāt pravartate gurur boddhā ca śatruś ca dveṣṭā ca hṛdi saṃśritaḥ
english: By his assent the action thereafter comes into play. He is Teacher, Knower, Foe, and Hater, dwelling within the heart.

sanskrit: pāpena vicaraṃl loke pāpacārī bhavaty ayam śubhena vicaraṃl loke śubhacārī bhavaty uta
english: Moving through the world by evil, this one becomes a doer of evil; moving through the world by good, he becomes a doer of good.

sanskrit: kāmacārī tu kāmena ya indriyasukhe rataḥ vratavārī sadaivaiṣa ya indriyajaye rataḥ
english: He who delights in the pleasures of the senses is, through desire, one who acts at his own will; but he who ever delights in the conquest of the senses is one who keeps to his vow.

sanskrit: apetavratakarmā tu kevalaṃ brahmaṇi śritaḥ brahmabhūtaś caraṃl loke brahmacārī bhavaty ayam
english: But he who has left behind vows and rites and has taken refuge solely in Brahman, moving through the world as one who has become Brahman, is a true student of the sacred—a brahmacārin.

sanskrit: brahmaiva samidhas tasya brahmāgnir brahmasaṃstaraḥ āpo brahma gurur brahma sa brahmaṇi samāhitaḥ
english: For him the kindling-sticks are Brahman, the fire is Brahman, the sacrificial grass is Brahman, the waters are Brahman, the teacher is Brahman; he is wholly concentrated in Brahman.

sanskrit: etad etādṛśaṃ sūkṣmaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidur budhāḥ viditvā cānvapadyanta kṣetrajñenānudarśinaḥ
english: Such, and so subtle, is the holy life of Brahman that the wise know; and having known it they attained it, beholding through the Knower of the Field.
